_comment: Documented-accepted security advisories. Run scripts/audit-check.mjs to validate the lockfile against this list. Each entry MUST include reason + review_due. CI fails on (a) any high+ advisory NOT in this list, (b) any allowlist row whose review_due has passed.

advisories.title: d3-color vulnerable to ReDoS
advisories.reason: Transitive via TWO roots (corrected 2026-05-31 audit): (1) react-simple-maps@3.0.0 (d3-zoom -> d3-transition -> d3-interpolate -> d3-color), and (2) recharts via victory-vendor's d3-interpolate@3.0.1 -> d3-color '1 - 3', both resolving to the same hoisted d3-color@2.0.0. Cascades into the d3-color/d3-interpolate/d3-transition/d3-zoom npm-audit entries plus react-simple-maps. Consumers: src/components/USMap.jsx (react-simple-maps, fixed brand colors) and src/components/DashboardGlobe.jsx (direct d3-interpolate import, numeric-only interpolation). The vulnerable regex parses color STRINGS; no user-controlled string reaches d3-color/d3-interpolate on any path, so the ReDoS vector is not exposed. Mitigation path re-checked 2026-06-07: react-simple-maps latest is 4.0.0-beta.6 (still pre-release) and it STILL declares d3-zoom@^2 -> the same vulnerable d3-color chain, so a react-simple-maps bump is a CONFIRMED DEAD END — the only npm-clean fixes are a breaking downgrade to react-simple-maps@1 or replacing the map lib entirely. Accepted on the not-exposed basis above; revisit at review_due.

advisories.title: Prototype Pollution in sheetJS
advisories.reason: xlsx 0.18.5 is the latest version on npm; SheetJS publishes 0.20.2+ only via their own CDN (not npm). EXPOSURE (corrected 2026-05-31 audit, finding M3 — the prior rationale's claim that Tractova 'never PARSES' workbooks was inaccurate): two paths use xlsx. (1) CLIENT export — src/pages/Library.jsx + src/lib/exportHelpers.js call XLSX.writeFile/aoa_to_sheet only (WRITE path; prototype-pollution-on-read does not apply). (2) SERVER scrapers — api/scrapers/_refresh-ca-dg.js, _refresh-md-dg.js, _refresh-va-dg.js, _refresh-nj-dg.js call XLSX.read() on workbooks fetched server-side. These DO exercise the vulnerable parse path, but only against fixed, pinned state-agency HTTPS URLs (not user- or attacker-supplied), so exploitation requires compromising or MITMing a .gov source. Residual risk accepted on that basis. Remediation tracked: migrate to exceljs (or pin the SheetJS CDN build) — revisit Q3 2026.

advisories.title: SheetJS Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
advisories.reason: Same xlsx 0.18.5 root as GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6. EXPOSURE (corrected 2026-05-31 audit, finding M3): the ReDoS parse path IS exercised by the server-side DG scrapers (api/scrapers/_refresh-ca-dg.js, _refresh-md-dg.js, _refresh-va-dg.js, _refresh-nj-dg.js via XLSX.read), but only on fixed, pinned state-agency HTTPS workbooks — not user- or attacker-supplied input. The client export path is write-only (buildExportRows in Library.jsx feeds Tractova-generated rows). Remediation: exceljs migration or SheetJS CDN pin; revisit Q3 2026.
